chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Kahmas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Have We not made the earth a container for the living and the dead?' He said: Burying the hair and the nails.

key_terms.كِفاتاً: A container or place to hold something

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by the earth being a 'container' for the living and the dead?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a specific exegetical insight into the Quranic term 'kifatan' (container/bed), extending its scope beyond human corpses to include bodily remnants like hair and nails. This establishes a jurisprudential basis for the ritual burial of these items, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining ritual purity (taharah) and honoring the physical body as part of the soul's connection to the earth.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Kahmas,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [77:25] Have We not made the earth as a place [77:26] For the living and the dead. Heasws said: Burying of the hair and the nails’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Faddal from certain persons of his people from abu Kahmas who have said the following: “About the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ’Have We not made the earth a collector (homes) of dead and living/ [77:25] abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’
It is a reference to burying of the hairs and fingernails/”
